result.title: Biological Congruence: Evaluating Microscopy Generation Across Representations
result.summary: Generative models increasingly produce realistic microscopy images, yet conventional evaluation primarily characterizes visual fidelity and distributional coverage rather than the biological information represented by synthetic data. We introduce biological congruence as an evaluation principle describing whether biologically relevant information forms a coherent description across representations and remains consistent with its empirical biological context. To study this principle, we develop a text-conditioned diffusion framework that jointly generates microscopy images and instance masks, exposing the same generated biological state through conditioning, visual appearance, and instance structure. Across prompt--mask, prompt--image, image--mask, and population-level analyses, we find strongly feature-dependent behavior: density and confluency are consistently preserved, morphology exhibits recurrent disagreement, while nearest-neighbor distance reveals that strong image--mask agreement can coexist with weaker conditioning and population fidelity. Stress testing increasingly unsupported phenotype combinations further shows that target controllability can increase while untargeted phenotypes reorganize and the complete generated state moves toward configurations better supported by real data. These findings demonstrate that generative quality, controllability, cross-representation agreement, and population fidelity capture complementary properties, motivating biological congruence as a relational perspective for evaluating scientific generative models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「生物学一致性」评价原则，用一个文本条件扩散框架联合生成显微图像与实例掩码，从提示—掩码、提示—图像、图像—掩码及群体层面考察生成数据的生物信息是否跨表示自洽且符合真实分布。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「同一状态在不同表示通道间是否一致」的评价思路，可能为核查 LVR 中视觉证据在内部状态与输出表示间的一致性、以及可控性与保真度互补关系提供概念参照，但领域为图像生成评价，与推理机制联系较远。
